If I could make one change to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I'd disable the new swipe-down gesture that summons Siri AI. There are already enough ways to invoke Siri, and doing so wouldn't disrupt my muscle memory for opening the notification center on my iPhone and iPad.

Meanwhile, on the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost all good news. Even as late as the end of August, new betas are still adding welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 ships next month, there's still one change I'd like to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes MacBook battery percentages harder to read

macOS 27 Golden Gate includes a redesigned battery control in the menu bar. By default, it doesn't show a percentage—just a battery-shaped visual indicator icon.

In that state, it looks fine. I also turned off the percentage display on my iPhone, which uses a similar battery indicator there. However, I've always preferred seeing the percentage on the Mac.

If you turn on the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number is placed inside the battery icon. I'm guessing this is to maintain design consistency with what iPhone does in iOS 27.

Putting the percentage inside the iPhone battery icon is a density solution Apple adopted to address the cramped space to the right of the notch or Dynamic Island. But on the Mac, even in the menu bar, I don't have that screen real estate issue.

I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15-inch MacBook Air since the first developer beta. I find myself generally paying less attention to the battery percentage, because it's harder for my eyes to see.

I hope Apple will reconsider this design decision going forward, especially if it's bothering more users. In the meantime, I've at least solved the problem for myself.

I used Codex to make a simple menu bar utility that displays the current battery status and percentage clearly, the way I want it. If you also find it useful, you can download and install it for free here.
